label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is a plain upright rectangular block in all ten views, with no sloped control face, base, or raised console top. A waist-high console needs more than a box, so the silhouette is there but clearly off the brief's form.

M2.reason: Measured 24 x 24 x 40 against a 40-unit height asked for, sizeOff 0, which is within 15% on every axis.

M3.reason: None of the brief's parts are present: no dials, no two screens, no row of switches. The sides, top and bottom are blank.

M4.reason: One uniform grey, mottled like concrete, covers every face. A console needs painted metal for the body and separate screen and control-panel regions, so the materials are wrong and there is no region variation.

M5.reason: No panel lines, screen glows, switch rows, dial markings or hazard paint. Nothing of the console's surface detail is there.

M6.reason: In the line-up it reads as a plain grey block beside Half-Life's rock, sphere and bone. A player would not take it for one of the game's props, and it is not a recognisable console.

M7.reason: It stands upright on its base, but with no features the front cannot be told from the back, so the front and facing cannot be confirmed against the original.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors, 12 triangles is far below twice the median of 62 for props of this size, and the box is closed with no open or inside-out faces.
